extra.reason: Fixed. A followed chain now answers the question the option asks in bytes: the engine keeps the wire truth (RedirectHop.RequestRaw/ResponseRaw, Response.Raw on the final response; hop requests rendered once so the scope gate authorises exactly the bytes the transport writes, hops sent via SendAs under the same rules as the operator's own send), the web layer maps them onto repeaterHop.request/response riding the send's own response, and the Repeater pane offers First/Final response plus per-hop 'View response' in the chain table — the chain is additive,  stays the operator's own. Follow-up fix the new tests caught: redirectRequest advertised the hop's Host as the bare hostname, dropping a non-default port — contradicts Burp's decompiled Zxrb.Zv authority rendering (host only for https/443 and http/80, host:port otherwise, IPv6 bracketed; :authority rewritten per hop on h2) and RFC 9112 3.2; hostPortFor now mirrors it. Evidence: sender tests TestAFollowedHopKeepsTheBytesItSentAndReceived / TestAnUnfollowedHopCarriesNoBytes / TestTheRawEntryKeepsTheFirstResponseBytesOnFinal, web test TestRepeaterServesTheChainHopsBytesAlongsideTheSend + byteless-refused-hop assertions; go build/vet/gofmt clean, whole-tree go test 38 pkgs ok, e2e-go.sh 24/0, e2e-ui 157 unit + axe green — e2e-ui's 8 failing specs fail identically at HEAD (bisected in a separate worktree) and are filed separately.

Fixed: all 8 failing specs resolved and the fixes verified manually in a real browser (agent-browser) as requested. Root causes: (1) RepeaterPage rendered hooks after its empty-state return — 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' killed every fresh-browser flow (5 specs); hooks moved unconditional, a4dd7d5. (2) renderTabTrigger's ContextMenu wrapper had no key — React unkeyed-children console error the suite asserts against (1 spec); keyed on tab id, a4dd7d5. (3) dock-persistence spec used a '.editor' class that exists nowhere (editor root is editor-shell) — spec fix 0a41a14. (4) proxyGet was describe-scoped but called from another describe — ReferenceError; moved to module scope, 0a41a14. (5) in-scope-only spec asserted an empty-state string the product never rendered ('this filter' vs 'these filters') — spec fix, 0a41a14. (6) decoder spec clicked Add inside a collapsed empty section; now expands first, 0a41a14. Product fix discovered by manual testing: a typed history query matching nothing claimed 'No traffic captured yet' while a seeded capture sat behind it — the typed query was not in activeFilterNames; now named, verified live in the browser ('No exchange matches these filters ... query host = ...'), a4dd7d5. Note: full playwright suite was interrupted at 218/1 (decoder spec) before the expand-first spec fix; unit suites green throughout (go 38 pkgs, UI 157).

Forward all shipped: engine ForwardAll (mirrors DropAll once-only gate + single signal, forwards held bytes unmodified — nil would wake the client to an empty message), POST /api/intercept/forward-all answering the honest count, toolbar button between Forward and Drop all with the queue-moved toast, no confirmation needed for the safe direction. Verified manually in agent-browser: 3 held -> one click -> queue empty, clients unblocked with own bytes, history rows present. Engine test TestEngine_ForwardAllForwardsEveryHeldMessageUnmodifiedAndCountsOnlyItsOwn, web tests, route manifest, UI unit 157/0 green. Commits: see forward-all commit on ui-react-comparison.

Shipped in 7b29220: Pretty view is editable; every keystroke writes back through compactMessage (message.ts), which inverts the prettifier — JSON re-stringified minified, markup collapsed back to the inter-tag breaks prettyMarkup inserted, head kept byte-identical, mid-edit JSON parse failure passes the operator's text through unchanged. The wire bytes, Raw and Hex all agree with the compacted body, so the 'reformatted body is not the bytes sent' objection no longer applies. Tests: 6 new compactMessage contract tests in message.test.ts (Pretty edit round-trips to minified bytes; edited head preserved verbatim; mid-edit JSON pass-through; pure-tag markup round-trips byte-identically and is a prettyMessage fixed point; multi-line text-node newlines preserved; non-formattable body untouched). bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect. Go gate clean.

Shipped in 7b29220: an unchosen editor (initial state 'raw' means 'operator has not chosen') now opens on Pretty whenever canPretty — Burp's documented default (tools/message-editor/text-editor.html: 'By default, messages are displayed in the Pretty tab whenever Burp detects a supported format'). The first explicit click, including a click back to Raw, wins for the pane's life via pickedRef — same deal Burp gives a pane once the operator has expressed a preference. A message whose Pretty view disappears falls back to Raw. bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail.

Fixed in b012797: the nav.palette note in shortcuts.ts:82 claimed 'Burp ships its palette with no default binding at all' — false; Burp's documented default is Ctrl+K, which burpsy already binds (defaultChord: mod+k, unchanged). The note now reads 'Burp's documented default is also Ctrl+K, so this matches Burp exactly'. One-line change; bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect.

Fixed: the claim was inverted. cmd/desktop/main.go IS a working Wails v2 shell with a native File/View/Tools/Help menu bar (buildMenu, main.go:151-203), native dialogs, and the console UI served via reverse-proxy AssetServer; verified it builds at HEAD (go build ./cmd/desktop). reference.ts's 'A desktop shell' entry said 'No native window and no system tray' — the no-tray half was true, the no-window half was false. The entry now states the shipped reality. bun run check 163/0.

Fixed in e8a8396: the status bar now renders the proxy listener address (stats.data.proxy_bind) as a live fact beside stored/exchanges/messages. Proven interactively on the live console (browser-driven, not Playwright): status bar displays '127.0.0.1:18200' matching the -proxy flag. bun run check 163/0.

Fixed in e8a8396: two affordances keep the empty-state promise — (a) clicking the already-selected connection deselects it (ConnectionRow toggle with aria-pressed), (b) a 'Clear connection selection' X button in the detail head whenever a connection is selected but no frame is. Proven interactively: relayed two real WebSocket upgrades through the proxy to a local origin, selected a connection (frames filtered), clicked clear (all 4 frames visible again), clicked the same connection twice (deselects). bun run check 163/0.

Closed STALE: the claim predates the held-row menu expansion. intercept.tsx:473-607 heldMenu() now offers Send to Repeater (copies row.raw to a Repeater tab without resolving the hold), Send to Comparer A/B, Send to Decoder, Copy URL/curl/to-file, Add host to scope, Open in browser, plus Forward/Drop. Only the Intruder handoff is absent, and :459-461 documents why it is deliberate: Intruder splices into a stored message id, which a held message does not have. Verified against HEAD 325905b by source read; no code change needed.

Implemented per the issue's option 2: Intruder consumes internal/bcheck's enumerator instead of growing a second parser. JSON bodies now offer one body_json_value position per string value (numbers/booleans excluded, matching Burp), payloads JSON-escaped so the document survives; base64/XML nested containers in body values arrive as body_nested_value with the outer wire value rebuilt per payload. Form bodies keep the existing wire-faithful walker; XML/multipart keep the entire-body fallback until bcheck models them (single-parser policy). Side effect: fixed a latent scanner bug — nestedDecode treated nestedBase64JSON as identity while nestedEncode re-encoded, so Apply corrupted doubly-encoded values; regression test added. Full intruder/bcheck/core suites pass; scanner runtime-coverage passes with the change.

Payload column shipped and verified: every attempt row the server returns names its payload combination — resolved server-side via payloadsAt over the post-processing-rule sets (Examples now covers attempt ordinals, not just bucket first-ordinals, bounded by the existing detail limit), rendered in the Results Attempts table as the second column per Burp's documented layout, with a browser-side ordinal-arithmetic fallback for ordinals the server could not place. UI lib tests (172), type check, Go web tests and a rebuilt bundle all verified. Blocked dependents pf4 (CSV export) and 4rd (sortable tables) stay open.
